subject: maths
question: Two trains having lengths of 100 m and 500 m are running at speeds of 100 km/hr and 110 km/hr, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
**Given:**

Length of train A = 100 m

Length of train B = 500 m

Speed of train A = 100 km/hr

Speed of train B = 110 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative speed

Relative speed (same direction) = Difference of speeds

**Calculation:**

Total distance to cross = 100 + 500 = 600 m

Relative speed = (110 - 100) km/hr = 10 km/hr

⇒ 10 km/hr = (10 × 1000)/3600 = 25/9 m/s

Time = 600 ÷ (25/9)

⇒ Time = 600 × 9 ÷ 25 = 216 s

⇒ 216 ÷ 60 = 3.6 min

**∴ Time taken = 3.6 minutes**
